problem: The mass density function $\lambda $ of a rectangular flat plate that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2}$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}.$ What is the total mass of the plate?
worked_solution:
The mass $M$ of a plate that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2}$ with mass density $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:      

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}{[-\frac{1}{x}]}_{1}^{2}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}(-\frac{1}{2}-(-1))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{y}^{3}}{6}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{3}}{6}-0 \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the plate is $M=\frac{4}{3}.$
